passage:
During an English test, students could use paper dictionaries, but not phones. Many students had never used one before.
They opened to the wrong letters, moved too slowly, and became frustrated. Their teacher had expected this.
After the test, she gave a short lesson on dictionary skills: guide words, word forms, and example sentences.
Students realized that a dictionary was not just a list of meanings. It could show how a word worked.
Phones were faster, but the paper dictionary made them slow down and think.
The teacher said, "Speed gives you answers. Skill helps you understand them."
